note: A screen, not an audit: questions worth asking and the data needed to answer them. No savings are computed; typical benefits are the cited sources' general wording.

questions.question: Are there more alarms per operator area than an operator can handle?

evidence.text: instrument PAH-101 reads "PAH-101 Fictional alarm candidate, not installed configuration" at U-A
instrument LAHH-201 reads "LAHH-201 Fictional alarm candidate, not installed configuration" at U-B

data_requests.item: Alarm rate, floods and standing alarms
data_requests.how: Count alarms per 10 minutes in normal operation and after upsets.

questions.decision_rule: Rationalize when the long-term rate or the upset flood exceeds the HSE guidance.

typical_benefit.wording: HSE: "the long-term average alarm rate during normal operation should be no more than one every ten minutes; and no more than ten displayed in the first ten minutes following a major plant upset."
source_titles: S23: UK HSE, Better Alarm Handling, Chemicals Information Sheet No. 6 (CHIS6, 3/00)

questions.limits: ISA-18.2 / IEC 62682 are not openly accessible; HSE CHIS6 is the citable open alternative.
